A1.justification: Both PDFs describe QCRD, with the same authors, central framework, and benchmarks. All pages, equations, figures, tables, and appendices were readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original T5-base and T5-small benchmark experiments, component ablations, sampling analyses, and rationale-quality evaluations.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark experiments and adds comparator results, discriminator-score analysis, negative-generator comparisons, and measured training costs.

M1.justification: Section 3.3.2 changes the specified negative-rationale margin loss from max(delta - CE, 0) to min(CE - delta, 0), reversing its contribution under Equation 3. This is a localized objective correction within the retained framework. Renaming self-play as self-adversarial does not establish another method change; implementation changes are not documented.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate SVAMP arithmetic problems, CQA commonsense questions, and ANLI1/e-SNLI natural-language inference. The added analyses use existing datasets and task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds the mutual-information method MI (Chen et al., 2024b) to Tables 1–3. It also adds Single-Task to the T5-small comparison in Table 2, where v1 evaluated only Finetuning, DSS, and QCRD. The existing comparators remain.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the reported batch size from 32 to 8 and margin delta from 4 to 3. New diagnostic protocols compare checkpoint lags 3, 5, and 10, fixed and teacher-derived negative sources, and discriminator scores at different temperatures. These reported changes do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds direct examinations of discriminator behavior (Section 5.5), positive/negative annotation imbalance (Appendix A.1), negative-generator alternatives and checkpoint sensitivity (A.2), and computational cost (A.5). These substantially extend checks of central design choices. Existing ablations and case studies remain; the relocated temperature analysis omits the temperature-1 result.

E5.justification: Section 5.5 and Figure 6 introduce probability-density estimation of sampled rationale-quality scores, absent from v1. This characterizes score distributions rather than uncertainty in benchmark accuracy. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for benchmark results.

E6.justification: V2 adds comparator, annotation-distribution, discriminator-score, negative-generator, and timing results. MI exceeds QCRD on T5-base ANLI1, 54.20 versus 54.00. QCRD's e-SNLI result changes from 90.15 to 90.26 in Table 1 and the training-size plot; revised settings prevent treating this as a verified same-setting gain. The temperature-1 result of 67.5 is removed, and the erroneous best-k statement is corrected from 5 to 1.

T1.justification: The margin-loss definition in Section 3.3.2 changes mathematically: under Equation 3's negative coefficient, v2 produces a positive hinge penalty instead of v1's negative penalty. This changes optimization direction and is not equivalent notation. The remaining formal framework is retained, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: contrastive distillation of positive and negative rationales, quality-based weighting, and improved student performance and rationales. Greater emphasis on diversity and self-adversarial generation does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive limitations concerning training overhead and dependence on prompt/decoding choices, while distinguishing training cost from deployment storage. It newly explains why teacher-negative rationales may still benefit smaller students and interprets discriminator-score distributions. Section 4.2 also narrows the T5-base comparison from superiority on all datasets to most datasets.

D1.justification: V2 supplies important missing reproduction details: learning rate 1e-5, 10,000 training steps, measured runtimes, task prefixes, discriminator max pooling, masking augmentation, and 500 discriminator-pretraining steps. These are newly documented details, not necessarily newly implemented procedures. The abstract promises future code release but provides no released code.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to MAGDI, mutual-information CoT distillation, and SCOTT. Related work more specifically positions prior contrastive approaches as incorporating negative knowledge through model inputs. The overall research positioning and claimed novelty of contrastive rationale distillation remain.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial portions of the introduction, related work, methodology, and discussion are rewritten. Section 3.2 is consolidated, terminology shifts toward self-adversarial generation, and discussion/appendix material is reorganized with a new Limitations section. The editorial changes extend well beyond inserting new results.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn, v1's MinMax illustration is removed, and v2 adds the score-density figure and appendix diagnostic/cost tables. The temperature case study moves into the main text, while the judging prompt and temperature-results table move to the appendix. Benchmark tables gain comparator rows and highlighted winners.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the paper by correcting the loss sign to match intended negative-rationale repulsion, testing generator alternatives and discriminator behavior, and supplying essential reproduction settings. The added MI comparison exposes an exception to superiority, while measured training costs and explicit limitations make practical claims more assessable. These gains outweigh the removed illustration and temperature point, although benchmark uncertainty remains unreported and the broad abstract claim is still insufficiently qualified.
